common_patterns.overview: Reusable patterns for governance-sync tasks. These patterns focus on preserving architecture, packaging, aliases, and validation while keeping edits minimal and synchronized.

pattern.name: preserve_first_review
pattern.description: Use when checking a repository surface for drift before editing.

steps.step: Read the smallest authoritative governance set that applies to the task.
Identify the affected files, scripts, aliases, and config surfaces.
Decide whether the change is safe or recovery-required.
Prefer the strictest applicable rule when sources overlap.

pattern.name: recovery_first_response
pattern.description: Use when damage is detected in scripts, aliases, config, or governance.

steps.step: Inspect the diff or changed artifacts.
Restore the removed or weakened behavior first.
Validate the repaired surface before continuing.

pattern.name: minimal_synchronized_update
pattern.description: Use when a governance change needs to stay aligned across mode and support files.

steps.step: Update only the smallest set of mode artifacts needed.
Keep the workspace mode and the supporting XML guidance consistent.
Avoid duplicating rules across multiple files unless a small summary is needed in the mode registry.
Confirm that the final guidance still preserves architecture and tooling protections.

pattern.name: narrow_validation
pattern.description: Use after edits to check the touched surface without widening scope.

checks.check: The mode slug is unique in .roomodes.
The new guidance file exists in the expected numbered directory.
No scripts, aliases, or constraints were removed.

pattern.name: communication_contract
pattern.description: Use when reporting progress or completion.
